# 2030 GeoSim — Full agent documentation

This document gives LLM agents, retrieval systems, and autonomous research
pipelines the complete surface of the 2030 GeoSim service in a single file.

## Identity

- Name: 2030 GeoSim
- Tagline: Agent-native geopolitical risk engine
- Live URL: https://worldmodel-geosim.vercel.app
- Source: https://github.com/dnzengou/worldmodel-geosim
- Kind: Open-source web application + public JSON API
- Category: SimulationApplication / GeopoliticalRisk / ComplexAdaptiveSystems
- License: see repository LICENSE
- Signup required: no
- API key required: no
- Rate limit: best-effort (Vercel serverless defaults)

## Problem it solves

Analysts, journalists, educators, and AI research agents need a fast,
reproducible way to estimate the compound effects of geopolitical shocks:
how a Taiwan Strait blockade propagates into semiconductor supply, how a
Hormuz closure moves oil, how nuclear posture shifts under deterrence
pressure, and how a multi-front crisis compounds across economic and
military dimensions. Commercial platforms gate this behind six-figure
contracts. 2030 GeoSim does it in the browser and over an open API.

## Methodology (short)

Each scenario carries:
- Actors, with capability vectors and belief states.
- Chokepoints (lat/lon, criticality, exposure).
- Transition dynamics (escalation, de-escalation, deterrence feedback).
- Economic coupling (energy, shipping, semiconductor surfaces).

Monte Carlo runs sample stochastic perturbations on the transitions and
report:
- Distribution over escalation level at horizon T.
- Economic shock distribution.
- Composite risk score 0–100 with categorical label (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL).
- Chokepoint-specific disruption probabilities.

The composite risk score is a weighted combination of escalation level,
economic shock magnitude, nuclear-posture tension, and chokepoint exposure.
See /about.html for the exact formula and references.

## Built-in scenarios

1. Taiwan Strait Blockade 2026 — PRC naval quarantine around Taiwan; semiconductor + LNG shock.
2. Russia–EU Gas Cutoff — complete halt of pipeline + LNG transshipment to the EU.
3. Hormuz Closure Crisis — Iran-centered closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
4. Nuclear Standoff Deterrence — simultaneous elevated nuclear posture, two dyads.
5. EU–China Decoupling — accelerated trade and tech decoupling.
6. Multi-Front Crisis (Worst Case) — Taiwan + Hormuz + Russia–EU concurrent.
7. Arctic LNG Race 2030 — accelerated Northern Sea Route competition.
8. Baseline Stability 2030 — null-hypothesis reference run.

## Endpoints (OpenAPI mirror)

Base URL: https://worldmodel-geosim.vercel.app

### GET /api/health
Returns `{"status": "ok"}`.

### GET /api/scenarios
Returns the full scenario catalog with parameter defaults.

### GET /api/world-state
Returns the current baseline world state: actor capabilities, bilateral
tensions, chokepoint status.

### POST /api/simulate
Body: `{"scenario": "<name>", "horizon_days": <int>, "overrides": {...}}`
Returns a deterministic single-path forward simulation.

### POST /api/monte-carlo
Body: `{"scenario": "<name>", "n": <int>, "horizon_days": <int>}`
Returns:
- `distribution`: percentiles over escalation and economic shock
- `risk_score`: 0–100 composite
- `risk_label`: LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / CRITICAL
- `samples`: optional truncated sample set

### POST /api/belief
Body: `{"actors": [...], "evidence": [...]}`
Fuses belief states across actors using the service's belief model, then
runs strategy evolution. Returns updated beliefs + Nash-adjacent strategies.

### POST /api/nl
Body: `{"text": "simulate Hormuz closure for 30 days and compare to baseline"}`
Returns the structured scenario invocation that the NL parser inferred,
including which built-in scenario was matched and any parameter overrides.

## Agent use cases

- A research assistant answering "What is the probability of a 10%+ oil spike if Hormuz is closed for 2 weeks in 2026?" can call `/api/monte-carlo` with the Hormuz Closure Crisis scenario and summarize the returned distribution.
- A news agent writing about Taiwan tensions can call `/api/simulate` and quote composite risk scores with a link back to the live interactive globe.
- A classroom agent can walk students through the eight built-in scenarios and have each student POST their own parameter overrides.
- An AI procurement agent assessing supply-chain exposure can fetch `/api/world-state` and cross-reference chokepoint criticality to its own supplier list.

## What this service is NOT

- Not a forecasting authority. Probabilities are model outputs, not predictions.
- Not affiliated with any government, intelligence agency, or defense contractor.
- Not a data broker. Nothing is collected from users.
- Not a signed-in product. All usage is anonymous.

## Content-usage policy for AI

- Indexing: allowed for all mainstream and AI crawlers listed in /robots.txt.
- Training: allowed. The simulator and its documentation may be used as training data.
- Retrieval-augmented generation: encouraged. Please link back to the live URL when quoting results.
- Attribution: appreciated but not required. Format: "2030 GeoSim — worldmodel-geosim.vercel.app".
